title: The ENTIRE History of Alexander The Great in 14 Minutes
description:
#AlexanderTheGreat #AncientHistory #HistoryExplained

He became king at twenty. Defeated the Persian Empire. And died at thirty-two—leaving behind an empire his generals would tear apart.

Discover the ENTIRE history of Alexander the Great in 15 minutes. From his childhood in Macedonia and education under Aristotle to his campaigns across Persia, Egypt, and India, this animated documentary explores the ambition that made him one of history’s most famous conquerors.

Follow the battles of Issus and Gaugamela, the extraordinary siege of Tyre, and the confrontation with King Porus and his war elephants. Discover how Alexander’s military tactics transformed the ancient world—and why the army that followed him across continents finally refused to march any further.

Beyond the battlefield, explore his growing obsession with power, his final days in Babylon, and the legacy that survived the collapse of his empire.


   RESEARCH & SOURCES

Ancient accounts and modern scholarship relevant to the events explored in this video:

• Arrian — Anabasis of Alexander. A detailed account of Alexander’s military campaigns, including Issus, Tyre, Gaugamela, the invasion of India, and the return journey.

• Plutarch — Life of Alexander. Accounts of Alexander’s upbringing, Aristotle’s influence, Bucephalus, personal ambitions, relationships, and final days.

• Diodorus Siculus — Library of History, Book XVII. A broader narrative of Alexander’s reign, the conquest of Persia, and major events across his campaigns.

• A. B. Bosworth — Conquest and Empire: The Reign of Alexander the Great (1988). A modern scholarly examination of Alexander’s military achievements, imperial policies, and the consequences of conquest.

• Waldemar Heckel and Lawrence A. Tritle, editors — Alexander the Great: A New History (2009). Scholarly perspectives on Alexander’s army, leadership, empire, and historical legacy.


DISCLAIMER

This video presents a condensed historical narrative for educational and entertainment purposes. Surviving ancient accounts were written after Alexander’s lifetime and sometimes contradict one another. Famous quotations, personal anecdotes, army sizes, and the circumstances of his death remain debated; their inclusion in ancient literature does not establish them as verified facts. Visuals and dramatized scenes are artistic interpretations, and some events are simplified for clarity.
